properties.decision:
RECORDED FROM BRAINSTORMING, THEN SETTLED THE SAME DAY. @ajs, 2026-10-10, dev_reflow2 hub session: "priority is doing the various phases surrounding getting reflow2 on to flo2.io. By the way, I've done so many things like changelogs and CI testing for reflow2, but what if we could drop some things to make this process easier to host the reflow2 design on flo2.io and just have a regular code repo (no design included within reflow2 repo, for instance). Would this make the transition from local reflow2 design committed and pushed to reflow2 github repo easier if we removed many of the requirements for what was placed initially on the reflow2 project/repo?"

WHAT WAS ALREADY SETTLED, so the question was narrower than it sounded: "no design in the repo" is the accepted end state (dec:idea-one-blueprint-the-store-is-the-design-and-an-export-is-a-perishable-photocopy, 2026-09-27; combined position 11), and req:ci-checks-the-code-against-its-design-on-the-server (accepted) says the per-PR gate moves to the server (position 9). What was open: how much of the machinery built for the copy can go, and whether position 9 can be cheaper than a credential in a public repo's CI.

WHAT THE COPY'S MACHINERY IS (all of it retires with the copy): docs/design/reflow2/ (54,600 item files), the design gate reflow2_check --export in CI, the design-only Python gates (intent authority, consumer reach, verification ratchet, self-host-uses-documents, item-layout merge tests), per-item lineage, worktree-private stores, tools/reflow2_design_copy.py with its one-PR hold (built this morning for the move), and step 6 of the release cut. What is NOT the copy's: the code tests, toolsnap goldens, the surface fixture, skill_lint, check_doc_versions, the CHANGELOG fragments (dec:idea-how-changelog-md-gets-written-once-the-design-is-the-record, 2026-10-03: CHANGELOG.md is a consumer document, written in a consumer's words).

OPTIONS:
(a) DROP IT ALL NOW: delete the copy and every design gate; nothing checks code against the design anywhere. SMALL work, LARGEST loss: drift between code and design is seen only when a person's session happens to reconcile; and the design stops being readable on GitHub while flo2.io designs are private.
(b) CI READS THE SERVER, THEN RETIRE (position 9 as planned): a flo2 account for CI with read-only membership, the design job skipped on fork PRs, then position 11. Keeps a per-PR gate. MEDIUM, and it needs a machine account flo2 does not have.
(c) STATUS QUO (c1) until 9 lands: the copy and the hold stay. Zero work, and the cost is paid on every design PR.
(d) A NIGHTLY CHECK ON THE BOX, AND THE COPY RETIRES: GitHub CI tests code only; a nightly job on flo2.io's droplet clones main and runs reflow2's own client (combined position 7, in build) against the hosted design, recording a Verification run with findings; loop_status shows the drift next morning. No credential leaves the box; fork PRs are unaffected. SMALL to MEDIUM: a cron and an ops script in flo2, one retirement PR in reflow2.
(e) DERIVE CHANGELOG.md FROM THE DESIGN at the cut (changelog_view, verified) and drop the fragments. Reopens the 10-03 decision.

AGAINST, KEPT BESIDE IT:
- A NIGHTLY CHECK IS NOT A GATE. A PR that breaks code-vs-design merges and is caught the next morning, on main, by whoever reads loop_status. For a project with one main contributor that is a fair trade; for outside PRs (#616 came from another team) the catch is later than today's.
- PUBLIC READABILITY ENDS. reflow2's design is public today because the copy is on GitHub; flo2.io designs are private and "make a design public" is planned, not built. The site's pages and the rendered skills-and-tools.md stay public.
- THE GATES WERE NOT WASTE. They exist because five cuts each shipped a different step wrong; the nightly run must report the same things (drift per file, claims without a passing check, the version claims) or the lessons are lost with the code.
- THE ORDER MOVES: position 7 first (the client that measures; without it the box cannot check files), then the retirement, then position 10 (a cut against the hosted design). Position 9 is dropped in favour of the nightly. req:ci-checks-the-code-against-its-design-on-the-server was REWORDED the same day on Anthony's word ("agree and concur on the rewording of the CI requirement"): a scheduled check on the server's box, CI testing the code only; so the CONTRADICTS link to it is resolved and records how.

CHOSEN: (d), kept by Anthony on 2026-10-10 as req:a-nightly-check-on-the-box-runs-reflow2s-client-against-the-hosted-design-and-the-copy-retires. (a), (b), (c) and (e) stay recorded as considered.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-10 — reflow2's repository becomes a plain code repo: the committed design copy and its gates retire once a nightly check on flo2.io's box runs reflow2's client against the hosted design (option d); CI reading the server, dropping it all now, and deriving CHANGELOG stay considered
